newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty back at resistance after intraday dip.
newsitem.headline: Zloty back at resistance after intraday dip.

text.p: The Polish zloty returned to just below the 2.5 percent from parity level after slipping slightly in morning trade as banks lenghtened currency exposure following a wave of position cutting on Wednesday.
"The zloty regained morning losses and again seems willing to drift sideways against the basket just below 2.5 percent and mirroring dollar/mark moves," said one foreign bank dealer.
The zloty closed at 2.50/2.45 percent from the trading band centre, a fraction stronger from Wednesday's 2.49/2.44 percent.
It closed at 3.1400/15 to the dollar, up from 3.1545/60 on Wednesday and at 1.8587/98 to the mark, down from 1.8482/94.
Banks cut currency positions on Wednesday to take advantage of higher-yield zloty deposits over the week-end, which set-off a $45 million intervention by the central bank.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates slipped to 21.68/22.1 and 21.80/22.18 percent respectively as banks wanted to place cash ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
Polish prices grew only 1.0 point in April with the CPI index down to year-on-year 15.3 percent from March's 16.6.
"Good April CPI was already consumed by the market after signals that price growth would be low, so the impact on T-bill yields should be small," said Robert Gluch of ING Bank.
Analysts said an interest rate reduction was not likely despite the steep fall in inflation because credit growth remained high. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
